plain_words.what: We cut the system into three parts, each one place where a word keeps a single meaning.
plain_words.decided: Three parts: subscriptions (what you want), billing (what you pay), fulfilment (what gets packed).
plain_words.assumed: 'Week' means the same thing everywhere. If billing and fulfilment ever count weeks differently, that is a new boundary.
plain_words.riskiest: A wrong cut is the most expensive mistake here: it is baked into teams, deployables and every contract after it.

terms.meaning_here: the menu choice for a week

decisions.question: Does billing stay its own bounded context?

options.summary: Keep billing as its own context that wraps Stripe behind an anticorruption layer.
pros: Stripe words (charge, intent, decline code) stop at the ACL; the core keeps saying week-charged
The Stripe adapter can be swapped or stubbed in tests without touching menu choice
Retries and failed cards are modelled once, in one place
cons: One more module for one person to keep alive
Every charge crosses a boundary that in practice is an in-process call
risks: A context that only forwards to Stripe stays thin and tempts people to bypass it
The ACL erodes if nobody writes a fitness test for it

options.summary: Fold billing into subscriptions as a payment policy on the subscription aggregate.
pros: Fewer moving parts; the charge happens where the week is chosen
No cross-context message for the most common flow
cons: Stripe types leak into the core model and its tests
Declines and refunds start to share a transaction with menu choice
Splitting it out later means rewriting the aggregate
risks: A Stripe API change forces a core domain release
The subscription aggregate grows into a god object

options.summary: Charge the card synchronously inside the choose-meals request, no billing context at all.
pros: Simplest happy path; one request confirms meals and payment
The subscriber sees a decline immediately
cons: Card latency sits on the hot path of the core flow
A Stripe outage blocks menu choice for every subscriber
Week cut-off and payment retry cannot be scheduled apart
risks: A timeout after Stripe charged but before we saved it double-charges without idempotency keys
Fulfilment never learns about a week that was chosen but not charged

decisions.rationale: Billing wraps a bought capability. Keeping it apart keeps Stripe vocabulary out of the core and turns the ACL into something a fitness test can guard. The cost is one thin module, which one person can carry.
would_flip_if: Payment rules turn out to depend on menu choice state, so the charge and the choice must share one transaction
No second payment provider or provider change is plausible within a year and the ACL guards nothing
